authorization.cap_scope: D022 is one aggregate campaign cap across both the earlier unsuccessful portfolio-dev account attempt and the authorized admin-learning campaign; it is not a per-account allowance.

reconciliation_snapshot_before_teardown.disposition: CAPTURED_NOT_RESOLVED; obligations are retained and are not represented as completed cleanup

cost_explorer_account_level_observations.note: EC2-Other was a data-transfer line paired with an AWS Data Transfer offset. This account-level observation is not resource-attributed.
Billing data was incomplete/lagging at query time; absence of a line is not evidence of zero charge.

cost.resource_id_grouping_note: Cost Explorer rejected RESOURCE_ID as a grouping dimension for this query, so realized campaign cost could not be attributed by instance/resource.

reconstructed_gross_price_estimate.rounding_note: Subtotal is calculated from unrounded usage calculations; displayed component estimates are rounded independently to four decimal places.
reconstructed_gross_price_estimate.compute_pricing_method: Observed instance lifecycles were priced using each observed instance type's hourly rate before aggregation; the dependency host is t3.small and application hosts are t3.micro.
exclusions: unattributed data transfer and service/API charges
billing ingestion and Cost Explorer lag

cost.cost_cap_assessment: The reconstructed gross resource-price subtotal is below the D022 USD 200 cap. Final invoice attribution remains pending; the estimate is not stated as the actual amount billed.

limitations: Application-host recovery only; this does not test database-host disk loss or database failover.
The network peer is a controller-started cold standby, not a continuously active second scheduler.
Recovery observations are bounded by the 30-second attempt lease and the 60-second fixture activity; do not quote them as general failover performance.
The tested activity is pure. Zero observed effect calls/duplicates is a workload census, not a test of external-effect deduplication.
Five global POISON_RECORD obligations were still OPEN at teardown and remain unresolved.
